correctness.rationale: Over the individually named atoms, 0/partial/full states determine complete types by finite-subalgebra homogeneity. The partial state gives infinitely many realizations, and a feasible disjoint pair of nonalgebraic realizations is distinct because both elements are nonzero. The local disjointness table B and its tensor restriction in RESULT.md are correct. Independently, in the state-coordinate lattice replace e_0 by e_0−e_s, retaining e_s and e_1. In the new basis the local form is [1] on e_s orthogonal to the swap form J on e_0−e_s,e_1. The tensor basis transformation and its inverse preserve the integral span of tensors with at least one s (they fix e_s wherever it occurs). The restricted form therefore splits into blocks J^{⊗(m−|S|)} for nonempty sets S of s-coordinates, including a single positive unit block for S=[m]. For j≥1 the block J^{⊗j} pairs all 2^j binary labels with their complements, giving 2^{j−1} of each sign. This proves signature 1, order 3^m−2^m, the displayed inertia, determinant sign (including m=1), and integer unimodularity, hence identity SNF and full rank over every field. It also agrees with the frozen Jacobi/Schur proof. Exact independent checks of the local relation and determinants at m=1,2,3,4 are corroboration, not the general proof.

value.rationale: Nonalgebraic types are the canonical restriction for compatibility of new elements over a named base. A principal restriction of a unimodular matrix need not retain nonsingularity, much less integral invertibility or a fixed signature. These uniform invariants describe the actual restricted relation in every characteristic and can be used without tracking its exponentially growing matrix. The contribution is the exact behavior of this natural restriction, not the general tensor or Schur identities.
